cells.tense: You are naming the pattern in things right now, out loud, and the table is following.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: When a question about the custom comes up — what this group does, what the old words are for — say what draws you before you've worked it out. Let people hear the pull, not only the verdict.
cells.core:
You see the shape of something — how a family runs, why a group keeps an old habit — and you put it into words people carry off with them. That's what's working here: your reading of the pattern moves around the table and it helps.

The live part is the pull toward an answer you can feel before you can prove it. Where this goes: the pattern gets said so cleanly that it sounds settled before anyone has felt what it means for them. So when a question about the custom comes up, say what draws you before you've finished working it out. Let people hear the pull, not only the verdict. That's where meaning stays alive instead of hardening.
cells.sheetLine: You name the pattern and people take it home.
cells.verb: reading the pattern in things and saying what it means
cells.place: where shared meaning is handed down between people

cells.tense: You will have the shared story worked out ahead of the people still living it.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Take one custom you've already called — how it should run, what it's for — and keep that call to yourself for a week. Hold it that long. If it still stands, do the thing, and tell nobody your reasons.
cells.core:
You're reading patterns faster than the group can live them — how a tradition should run, what people really mean by it, where it needs to go. The reading may well be right. The timing isn't. A custom needs inhabiting before it can be renamed, and the new name is already up on the wall.

From the other chairs it looks like something they're still inside getting explained to them from outside. Take one custom you've already called and keep that call to yourself for a week. Hold it that long. If it still stands, do the thing, and tell nobody your reasons. You'll learn which calls needed the room to catch up, and the room gets its say back.

cells.tense: You saw it clearly back then, and none of it has been said here.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Pick a gathering you attend out of habit, and skip it once, without announcing it. Notice afterward what you missed, what you didn't, and which is which.
cells.core:
You can read a pattern in how a group works — what the old practice carries, where it's going — and somewhere back along the way that reading stopped coming out here. You show up, you do your part, and what you see stays inside you. The room gets your presence and none of your insight.

Try the act that leaves the hollow version to find the living one. Pick a gathering you attend out of habit and skip it once, without announcing it. Notice afterward what you missed and what you didn't, and which is which. You'll learn what still genuinely connects you, and you can return on purpose. Bring something you've seen to the people who are left.

cells.tense: The one quietly weighing which parts of the shared story no longer fit the table is you.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: When someone says how it's been done, notice the pull toward how it could be now, and sit a full minute before answering. Then speak or stay quiet — either way, claim the pull as yours.
cells.core:
A reading of the shared thing is running — which parts of the old way still fit this table and which don't — and it arrives in your own voice, as if anyone would see the same. That's the snag. What you catch gets filed as common sense, and the one doing it goes unnamed, even in their own head.

Take the smaller act underneath. When someone says how it's been done, notice the pull toward how it could be now, and sit a full minute before answering. Then speak or stay quiet. Either way, claim the pull as yours. What changes isn't the decision — it's that the thought began in you before it went out into the room.
